children: Schneider National secured a new $350 million unsecured revolving credit facility led by JPMorgan, featuring a maturity to Sep 10 2031 (springing to Nov 22 2029 if its term loan is not extended, refinanced, or repaid), a $100 million letter-of-credit sublimit, and an accordion to $700 million. Interest is based on SOFR or an alternate base rate plus a leverage-based margin. Concurrently, Schneider amended its Nov 2024 unsecured term loan to align covenants with the new facility, and terminated its $250 million 2022 revolver with no outstanding borrowings. The actions streamline the company’s capital structure and bolster flexibility.
Agreement 1: Schneider National Lands $350 Million Revolver With JPMorgan, Upsize Option to $700 Million
: Unsecured revolving credit facility with $350 million commitment (expandable to $700 million)
: JPMorgan Chase Bank, as Administrative Agent, and other lenders
: Enhance liquidity and align capital structure
Agreement 2: Schneider National Amends 2024 Term Loan to Align Covenants With New Credit Facility
: First Amendment to unsecured term loan facility maturing Nov 22 2029
: Bank of America, as Administrative Agent, and other lenders
Agreement 3: Schneider National Terminates 2022 $250 Million Revolving Credit Facility
: JPMorgan Chase Bank, as Administrative Agent, and other lenders
